title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
This is a case of AI-enabled impersonation deployed to commit fraud. Scammers used AI-generated videos to create fake social media profiles impersonating a real immigration attorney, then used these profiles to solicit payments for fake legal services from vulnerable immigrants. The system was deployed without any verification that the person offering services was who they claimed to be, and social media platforms did not catch the fraud before victims lost money.

The failure happened at multiple points. The AI video generation tool was used without authorization to create convincing impersonations. The social media platforms hosted hundreds of fake profiles for months before removal. The payment systems accepted transfers for services that did not exist. No human verification of the attorney's identity occurred before victims sent money to scammers through WhatsApp, Venmo, Zelle, and Cash App.

It is not established who created the AI videos, how they obtained the attorney's likeness, whether the social media platforms had notification of the fraud before an anti-piracy company intervened, or what actions federal authorities took after being contacted.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of an elaborate scam involving artificial intelligence. Criminals have created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos impersonating him to defraud vulnerable immigrants. The fake videos falsely offer immigration services such as US residency assistance for $2,200 and testimonials from supposed clients who obtained legal status through his help. Leal first discovered the scheme last October when potential clients began contacting his office about these fraudulent offers.

The situation has escalated dramatically over the past three months, prompting Leal to hire an anti-piracy company that has successfully removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles across social media platforms: 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. The scammers typically direct victims through social media videos to contact a WhatsApp number, where they send phony contracts and request payments through apps like Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App. Leal is warning immigrants to verify the identity of anyone offering legal services online and plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate the source of the fraud.
